title: Cap. IV Arg. 3: beneplacitum de salute = praedestinatio — 1 Cor. 1:21 Credentes velle salvare
pass_a_gloss: Argument 3. The good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation: To will to save believers is the good pleasure of God concerning the salvation of men: Therefore. They say the Major is clearly true, because the very word of election signifies nothing else than God's good pleasure concerning the salvation of the elect man. They show the Minor founded in the Apostle's own words, 1 Cor. 1:21, It pleased God by the foolish preaching to save believers. Which they also illustrate from the contrary, Because God in men least believing does not have good pleasure, but his soul loathes them; and he swears that such will not enter into his rest, 1 Cor. 10:5. Heb. 3:18.
pass_b_english: Arg. 3. God's good pleasure concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation; to will to save believers is that good pleasure concerning men's salvation; therefore. They call the Major clearly true, because election means nothing but God's good pleasure concerning the elect man's salvation. The Minor they found in 1 Cor. 1:21 — It pleased God by the foolish preaching to save believers — and illustrate from the contrary: in men who scarcely believe God has no good pleasure, but his soul loathes them, and he swears such will not enter his rest (1 Cor. 10:5; Heb. 3:18).
source_text: Arg. 3. Beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem: Credentes velle salvare, est beneplacitum Dei de salute hominum: Ergo. Majorem dicunt esse perspicue veram, quia ipsa vox electionis nihil aliud significat, quam Dei beneplacitum de salute hominis electi. Minorem in ipsis verbis Apostoli fundatam ostendunt, 1 Cor. i. 21, Placuit Deo per stultam praedicationem servare credentes. Quod etiam a contrario illustrant, Quia Deus in hominibus minime credentibus non habet beneplacitum, sed anima ejus fastidit eos; juratque tales non ingressuros in requiem suam, 1 Cor. x. 5. Heb. iii. 18.
